rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban
No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
Register match.
Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Exercise file, not an article draft.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 49: gap analysis named as the move, no uncredited practitioner-specific technique used in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 86: "trifecta check" defined inline in the same sentence it's named.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a reference artefact capturing a user-supplied verbal frame.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No named practitioner cited in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No punchy overstated slogan needing a downstream carve-out identified.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms used (trifecta, AskUserQuestion, worktree) fit M4's arc position; trifecta explained on the spot.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Section closers checked cold; no dangling pronoun/demonstrative with ambiguous referent found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Past tense for exercise recap sections — heading and body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 79 "What happened:" uses past tense throughout ("You picked... walked... filled... settled").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No spatial/structural metaphor headers or unattached "other X" headers present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 86 "trifecta check" earned in the same sentence it's named ("does the agent hold private data, does untrusted content reach its context window, is there a channel out").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 86 uses "context window" precisely; no memory/context conflation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body.
Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No output-shape overspecification in body; prompt bodies live in the registry, out of this class's scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module. Compound-shape varies per module — never repeat same Debrief.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No Q1/Q2/Q3 retro shape; the maintainer block confirms no compound pass at this close.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lines 70-72 "Push back when a fill drifts from the codebase" is judgment-based collaboration correction (student's own domain knowledge catching drift), not systematic manual diffing of a long output for completeness.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not a self-study simulation file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All forcing functions run through Claude conversation (AskUserQuestion tool, prompts); no editor/terminal primitive introduced as the forcing function.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 66 names "./CLAUDE.local.md" explicitly rather than bare "CLAUDE.md".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 81: "## What closes the module" — noun-phrase header over a section whose body directs three student actions (set the return markers, run the trifecta check, paste the send-off prompt).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Lead with a command verb, e.g. "Close the module" or "Send the task off".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No inline markdown links present in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 40 uses bare "memory" in an agent-reads list (not a student-authored write); "skills you've authored" is unambiguous in context.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Ask Claude to..." for addressee/invocation, "the agent reads/ranks" for autonomous work — split holds throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No contemplative-pause prefixes or self-aware pedagogy labels; the "Time check" blockquote is pacing/room-sync info, not a reflection-beat announcement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
`.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No explicit file-save-as instruction in body prose (destination/format lives in registry prompt bodies).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lines 36, 49, 53: "You'll use it again next module", "You'll use it for every agent hand-off", "You'll see next module what the others were for" — student stays grammatical subject.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No per-module operational setting (thinking-effort, model, mode tag, slash-command) referenced in this exercise's body.
